label: D2 after choosing a2 (esp. when the previous trial was rewarded)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (zero at D1 and GO), almost entirely after the agent chose a2 (97% of mass; in_action==2 at D2), for both reached states (S2 common 73% of mass, S1 rare 27%). Within a2 D2 steps it is much more frequent and stronger when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward==1 holds 87% of mass). It does not fire after a1 choices, on rewarded-input steps, or at D1/GO. Dev: (phase==D2)&(action==2)&(prev_reward==1) P=0.87 R=0.76 F1=0.81 mass 0.85; the simpler (phase==D2)&(action==2) gets F1=0.80 with mass recall 0.97 but lower precision (0.69). Misses are mostly low-activation a2 D2 steps after an unrewarded trial. From the top example windows, magnitude peaks on the first a2 trial after a reward breaks a run of unrewarded or a1 trials, then decays over consecutive rewarded a2 trials (1.0 -> 0.68 -> 0.57); this is a qualitative read of the examples, not a fitted check. All variables are observable at D2 (the choice is known from D2 on).

issues: The basic claims hold. All activation is at D2 (D1 and GO are 0%). 97% of the mass comes on a2 trials, the a1 D2 steps carry 2.7%, and the reached-state split is 73% S2 / 27% S1. The in_rew==1 claim is true but means nothing, because in_rew is 0 at every D2 step.

The prev_reward modulator is a proxy. The real modulator is the PREVIOUS trial's reached state. Within D2 & a2 on dev: prev_reward==0 & prev_state==2 has precision 0.87, as high as the recorded predicate, though it was labelled the weak case. prev_reward==1 & prev_state==1 has precision 0.27 and mass recall 0.004. prev_reward==0 & prev_state==1 has precision 0.017.

There is a systematic false-positive class in the recorded predicate: a2 trials right after a rewarded rare transition (prev_common==0, i.e. the previous a2 trial landed in S1 and was rewarded). Precision there is 0.45 overall and 0.28 for prev a2 rare-rewarded, against 0.94 when prev_common==1.

There are also systematic misses. a2 D2 steps after an unrewarded trial that reached S2 fire 87% of the time, so 'esp. when the previous trial was rewarded' gets the cause wrong. Previous reward only correlates with the agent having reached S2 and repeating a2.

Better predicate: (phase==D2)&(action==2)&(prev_state!=1). It scores dev F1 0.896 (P 0.875, R 0.918, mass recall 0.969) and test F1 0.896 (P 0.876, R 0.916, mass recall 0.968), against 0.800 test F1 for the recorded predicate. prev_state==-1 only marks the window's first trial, where the previous state is outside the window. Most of the remaining false positives are on those rel -3 steps, where it is unknown, and the remaining misses hold 3.2% of the mass and look scattered. All variables in it are observed at D2.
The magnitude story (peaks on the first rewarded a2 trial after a run, then decays) was taken only from the top examples and never fit, so it is unverified.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after choosing a2 when the previous trial also reached S2 (fires on either reached state, whether or not the previous trial was rewarded; silent after a1 or when the previous trial reached S1)
